Findings: Trachea and both main bronchi are open. The main vascular structures of the mediastinum, heart contour, and size are normal. Widespread calcified plaques were observed in the aorta and coronary arteries. The thoracic aorta diameter is normal. Minimal pericardial effusion was observed. The thoracic esophagus is calibrated and no significant pathological wall thickening was detected. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were found in the prevascular, pre-paratracheal, subcarinal, or bilateral hilar-axillary regions. When examined in the lung parenchyma window; bilateral lung scarring fibrotic changes are observed. Scar forms that existed in the patient's February 2022 PET-CT are present in the posterior of both upper lobes. It may be compatible with TBC sequelae. Subpleural nodules up to 6 mm in diameter are observed in the right upper lobe posterior. The size of the large nodule has increased from 3.5 mm to 6 mm. No significant difference was observed in other nodules. In addition, smaller millimetric stable nodules are seen in both lungs. Minimal consolidation is present in the right lung lower lobe near the central peribronchial area. Impression: Bilateral lung changes, especially those compatible with TBC sequelae, minimal consolidation in the right lung lower lobe near the central peribronchial area, possibly pneumonic infiltration, minimally increased nodules in the right lung upper lobe anterior, atherosclerotic changes, and minimal pericardial effusion.
